newsitem.title: USA: Warburg revises 1997 zinc deficit to 90,000 tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Warburg revises 1997 zinc deficit to 90,000 tonnes.

text.p: Lower-than-expected mined zinc production in 1996 and 1997 has prompted brokerage SBC Warburg to revise upwards its metal market deficit forecast by 30,000 tonnes to 90,000 tonnes for 1997.

"Any reduction in Chinese exports below the level secured in 1996 are the result of ongoing western concentrate shortages, which should raise this deficit even further," Warburg said in its latest issue of zinc market update.
Several mines were shuttered this year, and production problems cut output at others.
Warburg originally forecast a $10 per tonne hike in 1997 zinc treatment charges for concentrates, but has now revised this to a rollover from this year's $190 per tonne.
Nevertheless Warburg's zinc metal price forecast for 1997 remained unchanged at $1,267 per tonne for average LME cash, compared to this year's forecast of $1,057.
LME cash zinc settled at $1,030 on Monday.

Commenting on market talk that Asturiana de Zinc's position, put at 200,000 tonnes by Warburg, has been sold to two large U.S. investment funds, the broker said, "If subsequently confirmed, we would view this development as strongly positive for the zinc market."

The development would indicate a substantially reduced risk from zinc inventory overhang as a large proportion of the estimated 9.1 weeks of stock would then be held by strong hands that would be far less likely than Asturiana to sell into any zinc price rally, Warburg said.

"In short, fundamental and speculative developments in the zinc market have only served to reinforce our preference for exposure to equities leveraged to this market rather than other base metals at this point in the business cycle," Warburg concluded.
